contract.goal: tell an audience defined by a rule - everybody, or everybody holding a role - something, as ONE stored document those people read and dismiss, plus an optional email broadcast driven from it
contract.output: notification-service only - CategoryClass.PLATFORM with a split bypass, the announcement aggregate with its audience predicate, one content row per supported locale, lazy dismissal markers, a recipient feed separate from the inbox, the targetable-role allowlist and category catalogue, a resumable batched email fan-out mapped onto the operation envelope, retention anchored on visible_until, and the mechanical checks from specs/enforcement-triad
constraints: no new in-repo dependency and no POM change
NO native SQL and no third fenced package - the visibility query must stay QueryDSL, which is why the feed is separate from the inbox (JPQL has no UNION)
the inbox read path must stay constrained by owner alone - no derived visibility term on the service's most-polled endpoint, and nothing in the inbox path may depend on the announcement entity
one row per announcement whatever the audience size: no materialized audience, no per-subject audience table
content rows scale with supported-locales, never with audience size
no second status enum for the fan-out - reuse OperationStatus, relying on the existing RuleGroup.OPERATIONS rather than adding a copy
exactly-once for a resumed fan-out rests on the existing unique dedupKey, not a second mechanism
the fan-out runs under job-core's RunLock, like digest and retention
a publish carries no channels and no alsoEmail - the category catalogue decides both
targetable-roles is consulted in exactly ONE method, and a rejected role must not reveal whether it exists
the category-class bypass stays exhaustive - no default arm
audit publish/correct/cancel through audit-core's single AuditSink; problems through web-core's one pipeline

decisions: groups live in the identity-provider-service, not here: org structure is already there (ou_id, organization), so ORG_UNIT arrives through identity-projection and is a separate change. Notification-local groups are a declared non-goal - a durable grouping is directory data, a one-off is already recipients:[...], and the reusable notification-only list is the one that rots because no leaver process touches it.

the feed is separate from the inbox for two reasons, the second decisive: a merged feed needs UNION which JPQL lacks, AND the inbox's correctness rests on the obviously-right predicate owner = me, so a derived visibility term there would be a materially worse risk on the most-polled endpoint (design.md D1)

visibility is evaluated LIVE at read time from the principal's roles - revocation works on the next read with no job. Same argument security-spring-boot-starter uses for projections over token claims (design.md D2)

email is a SNAPSHOT at publish and is a real long-running operation, unlike anything in the inbox: it runs for minutes, has progress and is cancellable, so it maps onto web-core's OperationResponse through its own run table (design.md D6)
PLATFORM bypasses opt-out but HONOURS quiet hours - a combination neither existing class can express, which is the argument for a third class rather than reuse (design.md D5)

localisation resolved with the user before tasks were written: one content row per supported locale, keyed (announcement_id, locale), rendered at publish with EVERY locale rendered before anything is inserted so a failing locale rejects the whole publish (design.md D7)

user committed add-in-app-notifications as 8164ef6 before this change began, so this change has its own rollback point and a separable diff. The two must not be implemented concurrently because both edit PreferenceEvaluator and the category vocabulary.

add-in-app-notifications is applied but NOT archived, so its specs are not yet in openspec/specs/. That is bookkeeping and does not block the code; both changes carry an enforcement-triad delta and those stack on archive.

1.4 evidence, verified not assumed: adding PLATFORM to CategoryKind alone fails the build in FOUR places (InboxItemMapper x2, NotificationEntityMapper x2) with 'The following constants ... have no corresponding constant ... must be be mapped: PLATFORM'. The triad check is real and now covers the inbox mapper too, which did not exist when the same evidence was gathered for ChannelType.

the bypass split is behaviour-preserving for the two existing classes and that is asserted rather than assumed: PreferenceEvaluatorTest.BypassMatrix has TRANSACTIONAL and MARKETING control rows, so a split that collapsed back into one question would fail them while the PLATFORM row still passed. Full suite 249 unit + 102 integration green after the change.

CategoryClassDto gained PLATFORM for symmetry but an announcement caller cannot choose it: an announcement names a CATEGORY and the deployment catalogue decides that category's class. Documented on the DTO constant so the next reader does not expose it as a request-level choice.

retention.announcement-ttl was added during 2.2 rather than 7.1, because the startup relation check (retention vs max-visibility-window) needs the property to exist. 7.1 will tick on the purge landing, not on the property.

AudienceKind documents what is deliberately ABSENT - ORG_UNIT and GROUP - at the point a reader would look for them, with the reason for each. The visibility predicate is written as a disjunction over kinds rather than two special cases precisely so ORG_UNIT is one more branch later.

the catalogue validator only runs when announcements.enabled is true, with a control test asserting a disabled deployment is not failed over a catalogue it does not use - same reasoning as checkLockLease only considering enabled jobs.

renamed service.model.AudienceKind to AudienceType and added repository.entity.AudienceKind, to match the codebase's dominant pattern ChannelType/ChannelKind/ChannelTypeDto rather than inventing a third suffix. tasks.md said AudienceKind in service.model; the rename is a deliberate deviation for consistency and is recorded here rather than silently.

check_migrations.sh caught a REAL hazard in 0020: a prose line began with the word 'changeset', which Liquibase's formatted-SQL parser reads as a directive - before the first changeset it rejects the whole changelog. Reflowed. This is exactly the rule CLAUDE.md warns about and it fired on the first attempt at writing it.

the announcement uses AuditedEntity's created_at/created_by/updated_at/updated_by/version rather than hand-rolled published_by/published_at: an announcement is caller-owned and 'who published this and when' is the first question asked about one, which is the same reason notification_request is audited and notification_delivery deliberately is not.

the shared ArchUnit rule entity-base.entities-extend-the-base-entity failed on the two @EmbeddedId entities. Resolved by extending AbstractEntity<CompositeId> rather than by switching to a surrogate id: AbstractEntity is a @MappedSuperclass declaring NO @Id field, only an abstract getId(), so a composite key is expressible through it and the pair stays the identity. A surrogate id would have permitted two rows saying the same thing and made idempotent dismissal a query instead of a constraint.

both announcement children CASCADE, which is the opposite of notification_inbox_item.delivery_id's SET NULL. The direction of the lifetime is the reason: there the delivery is purged first by design and the item must survive it; here the children are meaningless without the announcement. That is also what makes retention a constant number of rows regardless of audience size.

the audit category is AuditCategories.CONFIG with action config.announcement-published, NOT a new ANNOUNCEMENT constant: audit-core has 14 in-repo dependents, so a one-string addition would widen this change's gate to 14 modules. CONFIG is also a defensible fit - publishing is an administrative act that changes what every user sees. Promoting a category is a separate change against audit-core if announcements grow a surface of their own.

the audit record carries the audience as kind+value and NEVER a resolved subject list: the record should say what the author decided ('everybody with ADMIN'), not which particular people held that role that second - and a resolved list would be personal data in a record kept far longer than this service keeps anything else.

4.7 evidence, verified not assumed: injecting all four violations at once (a List field and @Filterable on AnnouncementEntity's audience, an AnnouncementEntity dependency in InboxService, and an Audience.ofRole call in DeliveryFanOutService) failed exactly the four new rules - 'Tests run: 8, Failures: 4'. All reverted, 8/8 green after.

the first attempt at the inbox violation used a constructor field, which broke InboxServiceTest's compilation and so could not demonstrate the rule. Re-done as a method dependency, which keeps the suite compiling and still proves the rule fires - worth recording because the obvious way to inject that particular violation does not work.

AnnouncementAdminController uses ROLE_NOTIFICATION_ANNOUNCER, deliberately NOT ROLE_NOTIFICATION_ADMIN: a notification admin inspects history and retries dead letters (operational work on messages other services asked for), while an announcer originates a message to the whole organisation. Support staff need the first and must not silently acquire the second.

two response types (AnnouncementResponse without the audience, AnnouncementAdminResponse with it) rather than one with a nullable audience: a sometimes-populated field is one line away from being populated on the recipient's endpoint, and that mistake would tell everybody the platform announces to which roles it addresses.

REAL BUG found by AnnouncementPublishIT: AnnouncementEntity extends AuditedEntity -> GeneratedEntity, so its id is DATABASE-generated. Assigning a UUID and using it for the content rows produced children pointing at an id that was never inserted (FK violation on every publish). The id must be read back after saveAndFlush. The inbox does assign its own id because InboxItemEntity extends JpaBaseEntity, where it is application-assigned - the two base classes differ and the difference is load-bearing.

audit assertions moved OUT of the integration context after two failed attempts. The platform already publishes a @Primary AuditSink, so a test-scoped @Primary substitution fails with 'more than one primary bean found' and takes 13 unrelated integration tests with it - both as a @TestConfiguration implementing the sink and as a split config. Third approach: RecordingAuditSink is a plain class used directly in AnnouncementAuditTest, which needs no context. Not a lowered bar - it asserts the same two facts (that record is called, and what the event carries) without destabilising a context the whole suite depends on.

SUITE-WIDE HAZARD found and fixed: each distinct @TestPropertySource creates its own Spring context AND its own Testcontainers PostgreSQL. Adding a second property-source variant (AnnouncementPublishIT, alongside SuppressionFallbackIT) tipped the cache into evicting a context, stopping its container, and failing 56 unrelated integration tests with 'connection refused'. The announcement catalogue now lives in NotificationTestBase's shared properties so the suite stays on one context. Worth remembering before adding a third variant.

SECOND REAL BUG, and the one this change's security rests on: LudwigPrincipal.roles() is ALREADY normalised to the ROLE_ prefix at the edge of the service, while the configured targetable-roles and the directory's security_user_role.role_code hold the bare code. The first visibility predicate compared stored 'ADMIN' against principal 'ROLE_ADMIN' and matched NOTHING - a role-targeted announcement published cleanly, reported success, and was visible to nobody, with no error anywhere. Found by writing AnnouncementVisibilityIT.

fixed by normalising ONCE, right after the allowlist resolve, through the platform's own Authorities.normalizeRole - so the allowlist still matches the bare code an administrator writes, and everything downstream of persistence (column, predicate, audit, admin response) uses the prefixed form. Rejected two alternatives: stripping the prefix in the repository needed a local copy of the ROLE_ convention because Authorities.ROLE_PREFIX is private, and keeping both forms alive past the resolver is how the two drift.

the fix is proved load-bearing, not assumed: reverting the normalisation fails four AnnouncementVisibilityIT tests with 'expected:<1> but was:<0>'. Restored. Two AnnouncementPublishIT assertions were updated to expect ROLE_ADMIN, with a comment pointing at that evidence - the behaviour change is deliberate, so the assertions follow it.

notification.validation.announcement.* keys were referenced by PublishAnnouncementRequest but never added, so every constraint message would have rendered as a raw key. Added in both locales. Also fixed a now-stale message: category-class.required said 'TRANSACTIONAL or MARKETING' and there are three classes.

5.1 is ticked on AnnouncementVisibilityIT rather than on a mock-based AnnouncementPredicateTest, and the reason is evidence rather than convenience: a QueryDSL predicate means nothing against mocks - such a test would assert that arguments were passed, not that the query is right, and would have missed the ROLE_ prefix bug entirely. The predicate is proved against a real database, which is the only place it can be.

phases 1-5 are complete and the first shippable increment is reached: announcements can be published, corrected, and read by their audience, with revocation taking effect on the next read. 286 unit + 154 integration tests green, coverage gate met, migrations conforming, validate clean.

exactly-once for the email fan-out comes from ATOMICITY, not from the dedup key: one batch creates its deliveries and advances the cursor in one transaction, so an interruption leaves nothing half-done and a resume has no overlap to reconcile. The existing unique dedupKey is the backstop for a double-run, and the batch idempotency key is derived from the announcement plus the starting cursor (not random) so that backstop is meaningful rather than decorative.

THIRD REAL BUG, and the subtlest: recording a NUMERIC attribute in an audit event fails the whole transaction at commit. AuditEventEntity is a SnapshotEntity with an immutability listener; the attributes map is persisted as JSON, a long does not round-trip to the same Java type, so Hibernate's dirty check schedules an UPDATE at the next flush and the listener refuses it. The error names the audit row and says nothing about the cancellation that caused it. Fixed by recording the count as a String, which is what every other attribute in this service and in IdempotencyAuditEvent already does. Two earlier attempts (reordering reads before writes) did not fix it; the type was the cause.

the layering rules caught entities reaching the controller: AnnouncementAdminService and AnnouncementEmailBroadcastService now return AnnouncementAdminView and BroadcastRunView, and the entity stops at the service. 3 shared ArchUnit rules failed (web.controllers-do-not-expose-entities, layering.layered-architecture, layering.controllers-do-not-access-persistence) and were fixed properly rather than suppressed.

AnnouncementEmailRunEntity extends GeneratedEntity, not AuditedEntity: 'who did this and when' is already recorded against the announcement, so audit columns on the run would be an emptier second copy and created_by would be whichever replica inserted the row. Lifecycle instants are explicit columns, as NotificationDeliveryEntity does for the same reason.
the broadcast runs at BULK priority so one announcement to the whole estate cannot starve the traffic people are actually waiting for - the priority lanes exist for exactly this.

the broadcast has its own RunLock name rather than sharing retention's: the two have very different durations, and a broadcast holding the retention lock for minutes would stall the purge behind unrelated work.

announcement retention is anchored on visible_until and removes announcement, content, markers AND the email run through one cascade - a constant number of statements regardless of audience size, which is the property the aggregate exists for and is asserted as a row count rather than a timing.

two retention fixtures tripped max-visibility-window, which is the validation working: computing the two window bounds from SEPARATE Instant.now() calls makes the window 30 days plus however many microseconds elapsed between the reads, against a cap of exactly 30 days. Fixed by using one reference instant with headroom - worth remembering for any future window fixture.

8.2: the two READMEs match 8-for-8 on the announcement subsections, and the three-class category table was added to both preferences sections. The one EN-only top-level section remains 'Build and test', which README.ru.md never had - pre-existing drift carried over from the previous change.

8.3: extended InboxOpenApiIT rather than adding a sibling, because the two contract facts a client cannot guess about announcements (cancel answers 202, and committed deliveries are NOT recalled) belong with the same kind of assertion already there. Still not a whole-document snapshot.
README test count updated from 340 to the real 458 (286 surefire + 172 failsafe), taken from build output.

gate run in full: manifest stale clean, image pins clean, migrations clean (16 changelogs / 90 changesets), mvn -q validate clean across every module, mvn -pl :notification-service -am verify BUILD SUCCESS across the whole reactor with all coverage checks met, 0 in-repo dependents, openspec validate --strict valid. check_api_baseline remains failing for the environmental reason the user set aside.
open_questions: should an expired announcement remain fetchable by id until retention removes it, or 404 when its window closes? deferrable - one predicate, no schema impact
should the fan-out emit a lifecycle event on the outbox topic as deliveries do? deferrable and additive; this deployment has no broker
